ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993 (NZ) for company registration, directors, shareholders, and registered office requirements; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35) and its Regulations for customer due diligence, beneficial ownership identification, PEP and sanctions screening; Company beneficial ownership data is supplied to the Registrar and accessible to competent authorities including the Companies Office, Inland Revenue, the Financial Markets Authority, and the New Zealand Police on a government-only access basis under the AML/CFT statutory framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the original Certificate of Incorporation before a New Zealand notary public. For Hague Apostille Convention member states, including New Zealand, obtain a Hague Apostille from the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs. This route is exclusive and must not be followed by consular legalization. For non-member states, apply for consular legalization through the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and the relevant foreign consulate; this route is mutually exclusive with the Apostille route and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Request the official Certificate of Good Standing from the Companies Office, have it notarized by a New Zealand notary public, and then either obtain a Hague Apostille from the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs for Apostille member states or proceed with consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and the destination-state consulate for non-member states. The two authentication streams are parallel and mutually exclusive; sequential chaining is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the proposed New Zealand limited company, authenticated by a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Have the Board Resolution and Power of Attorney executed in accordance with the company constitution, notarized by a New Zealand notary public, and authenticated either by a Hague Apostille issued by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs for Apostille member states or by consular legalization via the Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and the destination consulate for non-member states. These routes are alternative, not cumulative; never apply both to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company shareholders and New Zealand legal counsel, submitted to the New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute and notarize the Articles of Association before a New Zealand notary public. For use in Hague Apostille member states, obtain a Hague Apostille from the Department of Internal Affairs. For use in non-member states, undertake consular legalization through the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and the relevant foreign consulate. The Hague and consular legalization paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A New Zealand authorized bank with AML/CFT compliance obligations under the AML/CFT Act 2009
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the bank reference letter on the issuing bank's letterhead, have the bank officer or a notary public certify the signature, and then authenticate by way of a Hague Apostille issued by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs if the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille member state. For non-member states, use consular legalization through the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and the destination consulate. The two methods are exclusive alternatives and must not be used in combination.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every prospective shareholder, director, beneficial owner, authorized signatory, and material counterparty must undergo name-against-name screening on the New Zealand Police and Financial Markets Authority lists, the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Consolidated Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, and the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020 designations. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) must be identified at the 25% ownership or effective control threshold and for all officers under the AML/CFT Act 2009. Additional enhanced due diligence is mandatory for non-face-to-face applicants, shell corporate structures, and jurisdictions with known tax secrecy risks. Source of funds and source of wealth must be independently verified for every high-risk client, and all screening results must be documented, timestamped, and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Name Availability and Company Registration Portal (register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory names must be submitted in Roman/Latin script; English and Maori names are acceptable, but Chinese or other non-Roman characters are not accepted on the New Zealand Companies Register. The Companies Office applies a four-tier name comparison framework: identical matches, near-identical spelling variants, phonetic/homophone transliterations, and visually confusing or intellectual-property sensitive formulations. Any Roman-script transliteration that is identical or nearly identical to an existing reserved name will be refused. The legal suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' is mandatory and must appear exactly as required by the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a refusal notice from the Companies Office, the applicant must lodge a written reassessment request through the Companies Office portal within 20 working days. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may file a formal administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993, attaching evidence of prior use, trademark registrations, or ministerial consent. A further appeal to the High Court of New Zealand is available on questions of law only and must be filed within 28 days; the entire appeals process is strictly documented and must preserve the applicant's right to judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For refrigerated logistics warehousing under ISIC 5210 and NAICS 493120, a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable to Inland Revenue, the Ministry for Primary Industries, or trading banks as the principal place of business. Companies Act 1993 permits the registered office to be a physical New Zealand address maintained by a licensed registered office service provider, but that address cannot substitute for an occupied, temperature-controlled cold storage facility. The operating cold storage premises must be separately leased or owned, physically identifiable, and compliant with food safety and pharmaceutical storage licensing requirements. A virtual office may therefore serve only as the statutory service-of-process address while real operating premises sustain commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 45% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Ministry for Primary Industries within the first 12 months, and 35% probability by the local municipal council environmental health authority. Inspection checklist: (1) valid lease or ownership evidence for the cold storage facility, (2) operational refrigeration and temperature monitoring equipment, (3) HACCP-style food control plan or pharmaceutical storage protocol, (4) copies of utility bills demonstrating active consumption, (5) staff presence and payroll records, (6) insurer correspondence addressed to the site, (7) temperature logs covering the preceding 90 days, and (8) public-road access to a physical loading dock. Failure to satisfy any of these checklist elements will result in a penalty, license suspension, or cancellation of the operating registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee for a single-class non-listed New Zealand limited company with standard governance provisions.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Certificate of Good Standing from the Companies Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory certificate fee under the Companies Act 1993 for an official extract confirming compliance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and authentication bundle for five corporate instruments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand notary public; New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs for Hague Apostille; Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and destination consulate for consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary public statutory tariff plus DIA Apostille fee of NZD 25 per Apostille; for non-member states, MFAT legalisation and consular fees are charged separately; quoted as a fixed bundle estimate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT customer due diligence, UBO, PEP, OFAC, UN sanctions screening file

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), including sections 10, 12-24 (incorporation and company names), 28-38 (constitution), 40-48 (share capital issuance), 64-101 (share and ownership records), 128-138 (directors duties), 151-161 (appointment and removal of directors), 189-193 (accounting records), and 194-204 (financial reporting as applicable); also Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) application submitted through the New Zealand Companies Register; certificate of incorporation issued under section 15 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account rule applies under the Companies Act 1993. The company must have at least one share issued to a subscriber, and shares may be issued at no par value for consideration determined by the board subject to the solvency test. Non-resident ownership is allowed, but the company must maintain at least one director resident in New Zealand or Australia as required by the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD MEETING OF NZ_LTD. RESOLVED, pursuant to the Companies Act 1993 and the Company's constitution, and as a unanimous written resolution of all directors of NZ_LTD, that the following actions be and are hereby approved. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: The Board approves the subscription and allotment of the initial ordinary shares in the capital of the Company to the subscribers named in the share register, being the persons whose names and shareholding details appear in the incorporation application. The Board authorizes the Managing Director and the Chief Financial Officer to execute all share certificates, to update the share register, to file the initial shareholding particulars with the Companies Office, and to ensure that the allotment satisfies the solvency test and the disclosure requirements of the Companies Act 1993. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board approves the opening of one or more bank accounts with a licensed New Zealand bank and authorizes the Chief Financial Officer to select account types, execute account mandates, and appoint the following signatories: the Managing Director, the Chief Financial Officer, and any other officer named in the account mandate. All withdrawals, electronic transfers, ACH Direct payments, and Bank Wire transactions shall require two authorized signatories or a single signatory within the approved control limit, and all banking activity shall comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board approves and adopts the registered office of the Company located at the address set out in the incorporation application, being a physical address in New Zealand, and confirms that the office is open to the public during ordinary business hours and that service of legal documents may be delivered at that address until a further board resolution changes the registered office. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board appoints the individuals named as directors in the incorporation application to serve as the first directors of the Company, and further appoints one of those directors as Managing Director, one as Chief Financial Officer, and, if the Board elects, one as Company Secretary. Each officer shall exercise powers in good faith and for a proper purpose, shall keep the statutory registers, minute books, financial records, and tax filings, and shall maintain all statutory records at the registered office. 5. GENERAL AND REGULATORY AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the officers to apply for and maintain the New Zealand Business Number, Inland Revenue Department tax registrations including income tax, GST, PAYE, and Resident Withholding Tax, and all commercial licenses and permits required for the operation of a temperature controlled cold storage facility, including local authority resource consent, building compliance, Food Act or Medsafe licensing as applicable, Fire and Emergency New Zealand approval, and WorkSafe notifications for hazardous substances. This resolution shall remain effective until revoked or varied by a subsequent board resolution, and no person dealing with the Company shall be required to inquire into the authority of any officer conveyed by this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Pre-Incorporation Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online Companies Register and NZBN registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company name search through the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed name does not contravene section 20 of the Companies Act 1993. The name must not be identical or almost identical to an existing company name, reserved name, or a name used by a foreign company registered on the NZBN register, and it must not be objectionable, offensive, or likely to mislead. If the proposed name contains a restricted word such as Bank, University, Trust, or Cooperative, obtain written consent from the relevant regulator before filing. Verify that each proposed director is at least 20 years old, is not disqualified, and that at least one director is resident in New Zealand or Australia. Document the search result reference and the intended shareholding structure for use in the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name availability search confirmation
Consent to use a restricted name if applicable
Certified identification for each proposed shareholder and director
Proof of ordinary residence for the required New Zealand or Australian resident director
Proposed shareholding and subscriber declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried by the Registrar, submit a fresh name reservation containing a distinctive descriptor or request reconsideration by the Companies Office under its name grievance procedure. If another party objects to the name within 20 working days, file a formal response with supporting evidence of public recognition or prior use, or select an alternative name and reserve it immediately to avoid delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitution, Shareholder Consents and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial subscribers, first directors, and authorized New Zealand corporate services provider for onward filing with Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution in accordance with sections 28-38 of the Companies Act 1993. The constitution must set out the share classes and rights attaching to shares, the first directors, board powers, meeting procedures, dividend and distribution rules, share transfer restrictions, and provisions for officer indemnification to the extent permitted by law. Each proposed shareholder and director must sign a consent to act as well as a subscription agreement for the initial ordinary shares. Because the entity will operate a temperature controlled cold storage facility for perishable pharmaceuticals, include a broad object clause covering the storage, handling, packing, distribution, and logistics of temperature sensitive foods, medicines, devices, and biological goods, as well as the power to lease cold rooms, enter into warehousing bailment contracts, and apply for all relevant industrial and environmental permits.
required_dossiers: Constitution of NZ_LTD approved by subscribers
Consent to act as director for each proposed director
Share subscription agreement for initial share allotment
Registered office consent form executed by the office provider
Statement or declaration of shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar or a reviewing counsel identifies a defective constitution provision, amend the constitution by written resolution and re-execute it. If a consent to act is missing or undated, obtain a new consent bearing a date before the incorporation application and verify all signatures against passport copies before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Business Registry Group, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, through the online Companies Register portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application through the realme authenticated Companies Office online portal. The application must state the proposed company name, registered office address, principal place of business, full names, addresses, dates and places of birth of directors and shareholders, the share structure, and the date of incorporation requested. Attach the constitution if adopted and all signed consents. Make the statutory declaration that the company will comply with the Companies Act 1993 and that the information is true and accurate. Pay the applicable state filing fee using the online payment gateway. Upon successful validation, the Companies Office will issue a certificate of incorporation and the NZBN will be automatically generated and linked to the company. Retain the certificate and company extract for bank account opening, tax registrations, and industrial licensing applications.
required_dossiers: Completed incorporation application form through Companies Register portal
Certificate of name search confirmation
Adopted constitution
Consent to act as director for each director
Consent to use registered office
Proof of payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or flagged for incomplete information, use the Companies Office dashboard to respond to the requisition within 15 working days. Correct any identity verification issues by uploading clearer certified copies of passports or proof of address. If the Registrar refuses registration, request a written statement of reasons and appeal to the High Court under the judicial review procedure while simultaneously preparing a corrected application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Tax Registrations and Maintenance of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Inland Revenue Department, New Zealand Companies Office, NZBN Register, and the board of directors of NZ_LTD
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ten working days of incorporation, hold the first board meeting or execute a unanimous written resolution adopting the pro-forma first board resolution. Register the company with Inland Revenue for income tax and elect a balance date. Register for GST on the Companies Office GST application platform or through IRD Business OnLine if the twelve-month turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000. Register for PAYE if the company will employ workers. Prepare the statutory registers required by the Companies Act 1993, including the register of shares, register of directors, register of shareholders, accounting records, and minute book. File the NZBN details and any overseas ownership declarations required under the Companies Act or Anti-Money Laundering rules. If the company will employ staff, also register as an employer with Inland Revenue and the Accident Compensation Corporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN confirmation
IRD income tax registration confirmation
GST and PAYE registration forms if applicable
Board resolution and minute book
Share register and director register
Share certificate templates
ACorporation employer registration or contracting status evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue rejects or queries the tax registrations due to a mismatch in director identity or Australian tax residency status, file a correction notice with a statutory declaration and certified passports. If the company misses a filing deadline, contact Inland Revenue promptly, explain the reasonable cause, and submit the required return before a penalty assessment is finalized. For Companies Office annual return or record queries, update the register through the Companies Office Manage Company portal within the time stated in the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Anti-Money Laundering KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand registered bank and the Company's AML/CFT compliance function
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certificate of incorporation and NZBN, open the company's operating bank account at a licensed New Zealand bank. Provide the bank with the certificate of incorporation, the company constitution, the board resolution authorizing account opening and signatories, certified passports of the directors and beneficial owners, proof of residential address, and evidence of the physical cold storage premises lease or ownership for the bank's customer due diligence. Complete the AML/CFT customer risk assessment, including expected monthly turnover, counterparties in the cold chain, and source of funds for initial share capital. Set up ACH Direct and Bank Wire payment rails for the warehousing business. The bank may also request a letter from the external accountant confirming the intended use of the account and that no politically exposed persons are involved unless otherwise disclosed.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
NZBN registration certificate
Bank signatory appointment resolution
Passport and proof of address for each signatory
Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration
Proof of cold storage facility premises and business plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional information, supply the requested documents within five business days with certified English translations where necessary. If the application is declined on unsatisfactory KYC grounds, submit a fresh application to another licensed bank using the same corrected data pack. If the bank's refusal appears unlawful, raise a complaint with the Internal Complaints Resolution process and refer the matter to the Banking Ombudsman.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) and the relevant territorial authority such as Auckland Council, together with Medsafe, WorkSafe New Zealand, and Fire and Emergency New Zealand
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cold Chain Logistics Facility Operating Approval under the Food Act 2014 and the Medicines Act 1981 wholesale distribution/storage Good Distribution Practice certificate; ancillary resource consent for industrial cold storage under the Resource Management Act 1991.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) and the relevant Regional Council under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Resource consent with a formal Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE) is required for an industrial cold storage facility using ammonia-based refrigeration systems above the hazardous substances location thresholds. For smaller systems, the activity may be classified as a Controlled Activity with environmental registration only; for larger ammonia inventories or facilities within a sensitive zone, classification rises to Restricted Discretionary or Non-Complying Activity requiring a full AEE.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Discharges to stormwater must not exceed 0.5 mg/L ammonia nitrogen; process wastewater introduced to municipal sewer must meet the regional tradewaste limits, generally pH 6-9, biochemical oxygen demand BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 350 mg/L, and ammoniacal nitrogen not exceeding 25 mg/L unless a tradewaste consent increases the allowance. Refrigerant gas losses must comply with the ozone protection and climate change regulations, and halogenated refrigerants with GWP above 150 must be phased down according to the regulated profiled schedule. Hazardous waste must be stored in bundled, impervious areas and removed by a licensed waste carrier.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand approval of the Fire Safety and Evacuation Scheme under the Fire and Emergency Act 2017, building warrant of fitness and compliance schedule under the Building Act 2004, annual inspection of emergency lighting, sprinklers, fire extinguishers, and refrigeration machine room gas detection, structural load inspection for the racking and floor system, and WorkSafe New Zealand certification of the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 plan including hazardous substances location certificate for ammonia refrigeration. A hot work permit and fire safety certificate must be maintained for any maintenance operations creating ignition risk.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Tāke) of New Zealand; secure online portal: myIR (myIR Secure Online Services). Corporate registry interface: New Zealand Companies Office / New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand incorporated limited company, the Registrar of Companies supplies company registration data to Inland Revenue and the company is issued an IRD number; the IRD number is confirmed and administered through myIR. If a separate non-resident company must obtain its own tax identifier, the non-resident entity must apply through Inland Revenue's myIR portal for an IRD number as a non-resident company, submitting: (i) certified certificate of incorporation or equivalent registration document from the home jurisdiction; (ii) constitution or governing documents; (iii) complete register of directors and ultimate beneficial owners; (iv) New Zealand address for service or registered agent; (v) declaration of non-residence and tax residency status; and (vi) intended New Zealand business and GST activities. Any application to register for GST may be made simultaneously in myIR, selecting the appropriate GST registration effective date and filing frequency. The IRD number is the statutory taxpayer identification used for all New Zealand GST, income tax, and PAYE obligations; the NZBN is a separate business identifier and does not replace the IRD number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A New Zealand limited company is a separate legal and taxpaying entity under the Companies Act 1993 and the Income Tax Act 2007. The company is subject to entity-level taxation at the prevailing New Zealand corporate income tax rate; the shareholder is not taxed directly on the company's income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for this entity configuration. New Zealand has no check-the-box election. A New Zealand close company may elect look-through company (LTC) status under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, but a standard limited company (NZ_LTD) is not eligible for LTC treatment unless it meets ownership and resident requirements and files an election. No hybrid mismatch election is available; the hybrid mismatch rules under sections FH 1-FH 11 of the Income Tax Act 2007 apply automatically.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000: a person must register for GST if the value of taxable supplies made in New Zealand exceeded or is expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period (Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, section 51). Registration is voluntary below this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime applies in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and interoperable through the New Zealand e-Invoicing Network (Peppol-based PEPPOL network run with MBIE). GST returns are filed electronically through myIR, and invoice-level reporting is not required. Invoices must satisfy the content requirements of section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, and business records must be preserved under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 when they are physically exported from New Zealand by the supplier in the same or substantially the same condition as at the time of supply, and export occurs within the statutory time frame (generally within 28 days of the time of supply; certain non-resident purchaser scenarios allow removal within 60 days). Services may be zero-rated under section 11(1)(b) where the recipient is a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and the supply is not connected with New Zealand land or moveable personal property physically situated in New Zealand. For this cold-chain logistics operation, warehousing and controlled-temperature storage of pharmaceuticals physically located in New Zealand is generally a taxable supply at 15% GST; zero-rating may apply only to the separately identifiable international transport or qualifying offshore services, and contemporaneous export evidence must be retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service export entry lodged through the Trade Single Window (approved EDI/declaration manifest for departure clearance)
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) naming the exporter and consignee
Commercial invoice and packing list evidencing the exported pharmaceuticals
Warehouse release / cold-chain temperature logs and pharmaceutical handling records substantiating physical removal from New Zealand
Bank foreign exchange credit advice (SWIFT MT103 or corresponding bank confirmation) showing the export proceeds credited to the New Zealand company's account
GST working papers and zero-rating reconciliation schedules supporting the 0% treatment on the GST return
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may deny zero-rating and assess GST at 15% if the exported goods or offshore service criteria are not supported by adequate records. The Tax Administration Act 1994 imposes use-of-money interest from the original due date and shortfall penalties of 20% for lack of reasonable care or unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, and 100% for abusive tax positions; fraudulent or intentionally misleading export/zero-rating claims can also lead to criminal prosecution and assessments outside the normal four-year time bar. Although New Zealand does not impose a specific statutory 180-day export proceeds repatriation limit, the banking/foreign-exchange confirmation should evidence receipt within that benchmark to preserve a contemporaneous audit trail.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a structurally open financial system. The New Zealand dollar is independently floated since 1985 and trades freely against all major currencies in spot, forward, swap and option markets. There are no exchange control licenses, no capped conversion thresholds, and no pre-approval requirement from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand for current account or capital account transactions. The current and capital accounts are effectively fully convertible for residents and non-residents, subject only to overseas investment screening in sensitive land and significant business assets under the Overseas Investment Act 2005. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal; non-resident shareholders may receive dividends with applicable withholding taxes, and double taxation agreements can reduce these rates upon submission of a certificate of residence. Exporters are not required to convert earnings into NZD; proceeds may be retained in any permitted currency. The practical frictions in New Zealand are therefore banking counterparty due-diligence, AML/CFT verification and corporate documentation, rather than state-imposed foreign exchange restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender rules exist under New Zealand law. Exporters are permitted to hold foreign currency proceeds in external accounts indefinitely, may use them directly for import settlements, and there is no mandatory conversion ratio or timeframe imposed by the Reserve Bank. The only compliance obligation is the standard tax treatment of foreign currency gains or losses, requiring conversion to NZD for financial statements and tax reporting, with any repatriation made at the commercial wholesale rate quoted by the registered bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Clearing Account for SWIFT MT103

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs are not licensed as banks in New Zealand and cannot provide direct participation in the Exchange Settlement Account System operated through the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, any provider of money changing or remittance services must be registered and supervised by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs or the Financial Markets Authority. Most offshore EMIs hold no New Zealand registration and therefore cannot issue local account numbers, accept local electronic transfers, or support statutory corporate banking requirements. Use of an offshore EMI for primary treasury clearing is legally exposed to unregistered financial service provider objections from external auditors and local banks. The viability is rated Low for capital escrow, trade settlement and clearing rails; at most it can act as a supplementary pass-through for non-core receivables, and even then only where the EMI is a registered reporting entity under the AML/CFT regime.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors are not legally required to appear physically in a New Zealand bank branch. Each registered bank may accept virtual video identification, notarised passport copies, apostilled corporate documentation, and remote identity confirmation under the AML/CFT Act, provided that additional verification of the director address and the company operating address is completed. In practice, ANZ, BNZ, ASB and Westpac will require at least one formal video interview with the authorised signatory director. A consular proxy opening is not a statutory right; instead, a notarised power of attorney or certified resolution passed in the presence of a justice of the peace or notary can be used. For the cold storage entity, the bank will additionally require proof of the physically operating warehouse site, including a lease agreement and council rates letter, before the high-risk business banking review is completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear natural-person controller where shares are held through a discretionary trust, nominee arrangement or a foreign holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trust deed or certified extract, overseas trust tax residency certificate, register of ultimate beneficial owners identifying every trustee, settlor and protector, identity of all discretionary beneficiaries or class definition, certified share registers, notarised passports of the final beneficial owners, independent verification of source of wealth with audited financial statements covering at least the last three years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection amount inconsistent with the stated trade cycle of temperature-controlled cold storage operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited parent company financials for three years, six months of prior bank statements showing the funds were accumulated in a regulated bank, the signed share subscription and allotment agreement, the underlying warehouse lease or acquisition contract, valuation certificate of refrigerated equipment, and a notarised sworn affidavit from the settlor or source of funds confirming the commercial origin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected counterparty payment flows from the cold storage logistics chain route through jurisdictions considered higher risk or arising from third-party logistics invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements with each logistics counterparty, individual counterparty KYC packs including their business registration and financial statements, purchase order and goods receive dockets, temperature monitoring logs for perishable pharmaceuticals, bills of lading and customs summary declarations, and open-source or subscription-based due diligence reports such as World-Check or equivalent on each known supplier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent tax or Companies Office data between the applicant entity and the bank presentation package.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current certificate of incorporation issued by the New Zealand Companies Office, the latest Companies Office company extract, IRD number confirmation letter for the entity, IR361 tax status letter where relevant, board resolution authorising the banking mandate and signatories, certified copies of passports of each signatory, and the signed bank mandate in the exact exact entity name covering all legal variations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital should be directed to the NZ registered bank receiving account using a SWIFT MT103 from the investor's regulated bank, with the beneficiary account named precisely as the New Zealand limited company. The remittance must reference the share allotment or capital contribution, and the purpose should be classified as direct investment equity capital to the treasury team. The bank will verify the originator bank correspondent chain and may request a certified copy of the board resolution approving the capital injection. After receipt, the company must update the Companies Office share register and provide a capital verification certificate from the external auditor if the funds are held in a dedicated capital escrow account. Where the investor is in a jurisdiction with a foreign exchange regime, the local outbound bank must obtain its own central bank approval; the New Zealand receiving bank does not impose further surrender requirements.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: For monthly temperature-controlled warehousing fees and utility disbursements, direct SWIFT MT103 payment rails are appropriate. For large pharmaceutical cold chain procurement, an irrevocable confirmed documentary letter of credit issued through the New Zealand bank is preferred, with the bill of lading, pharma temperature record, and packing list attached. Documentary collections such as D/P or D/A may be used where a long-established trading relationship exists, but will require the underlying supply contract and insurance certificate to be presented to the confirming bank. All export and import settlements must maintain an audit trail matching the New Zealand IRD tax invoice requirements, and any abnormal third-country flow will be queried by the bank as a potential trade-based money laundering signal.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable FX forwards up to 12 months in AUD, USD, EUR, GBP, JPY and CNY for hedging trade receivables and import payables.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted or non-fully-convertible Asian currencies, including offshore CNY, IDR, PHP, VND, THB and KRW, under an appropriate ISDA/CSA master agreement with the bank treasury.
FX swaps between NZD and major clearing currencies for short-term working capital bridge conversions, subject to standard counterparty credit limits.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term NZD-denominated borrowing where the underlying asset is a foreign currency capital contribution, documented under an ISDA master agreement and cleared or reported in line with relevant domestic derivative regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Annual Return under Companies Act 1993, sections 209-216
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual return must be filed no later than 30 working days after the company's annual return date, being the anniversary of the date of incorporation; the filing window opens three months before that anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual return triggers a Registrar reminder and subsequent default notice; continued non-filing is a statutory ground for administrative strike-off and dissolution under Companies Act 1993 section 318(1)(c). A struck-off company loses legal personality, cannot trade or contract, and restoration requires backfiling, payment of arrears and restoration fees, and possible Court involvement; directors may be disqualified and may become personally liable for debts incurred after strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Auditor's Report, applicable only if the company is a statutory large entity or an FMC reporting entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; Financial Markets Authority for FMC reporting entities; audited financial statements must also be provided to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared, approved and signed by directors within 5 months after balance date and lodged with the Companies Office within 20 working days after the date of signature; for a standard 31 March balance date, this means lodgement by the September/October filing window in extreme cases, assuming the maximum statutory timeline is used.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare, sign, audit or file annual financial statements is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, carrying corporate fines of up to NZD 50,000 and director fines of up to NZD 10,000; the Registrar may also issue infringement notices, require corrected statements, and proceed to deregistration for persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return, Inland Revenue form IR4, including annual financial statements or tax reconciliation annexure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 company return is due on 31 May if filed without a tax agent, or on 7 July if filed by an approved tax agent; for an approved alternative balance date, the return is due within 1 month after balance date without an agent, or within 3 to 4 months after balance date with an agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts an initial late filing penalty of NZD 250, automated daily late filing penalties of NZD 50 per day for up to 50 days, use-of-money interest on unpaid tax, default assessment powers, and IRD debt recovery; in egregious cases, directors may face personal liability proceedings for unpaid tax obligations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is mandatory for any New Zealand company that is a statutory large entity under Financial Reporting Act 2013 section 45: in each of the two immediately preceding accounting periods, total assets exceed NZD 60 million, or total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million, or the company has 50 or more full-time equivalent employees. A statutory audit is also mandatory for every FMC reporting entity, including listed issuers, managed investment schemes and financial services providers, regardless of size, and for any company whose constitution or shareholder or lender agreement requires an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand GAAP as established by the External Reporting Board under the Financial Reporting Act 2013: Tier 1 for-profit entities apply New Zealand Equivalents to IFRS, Tier 2 entities apply NZ IFRS with the Reduced Disclosure Regime, and Tier 3 and Tier 4 small and medium for-profit entities apply the XRB Simple Format Reporting standards, being NZ SAE for accrual entities and NZ SFM for reporting under simple formats.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate public UBO annual return for an ordinary private limited company. The Companies Act 1993 annual return is the annual confirmation event, confirming the registered office, service address, all directors, share classes, and all shareholders. An allotment of new shares must be delivered to the Companies Office within 20 working days of allotment, whereas a transfer of existing shares is recorded immediately in the company's own register of members and is then captured in the next annual return; there is no 30-day transfer filing window for existing share transfers. Under the AML/CFT Act 2009, if the entity is a financial service provider or designated non-financial business, it must identify, verify and periodically refresh beneficial ownership information as part of customer due diligence, but no public UBO filing is required by the Companies Office.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 900 per annum for a New Zealand registered office and company secretarial provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 40,000 for a statutory audit of a mid-size New Zealand company; entities below the large-entity thresholds will not incur a compulsory audit fee and can rely on exemption rules.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No preferential corporate tax zone or patent box applies to ISIC 5210 temperature-controlled cold storage in New Zealand. Relevant effective tax relief includes the refundable 15% R&D tax credit under Income Tax Act 2007 sections LY 1 to LY 11, the Approved Issuer Levy at 2% for eligible interest paid to non-residents through approved issuers, depreciation on refrigeration and warehouse assets, immediate expensing of low-value assets below NZD 5,000, and indefinite tax loss carry-forward subject to the 49% shareholder continuity test. Cold storage revenue is taxed at the standard 28% company rate without any free-zone concession.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (statutory carry-forward without expiry, subject to the 49% shareholder continuity requirement)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Inland Revenue Form IR4 (Company Income Tax Return), filed through Inland Revenue's myIR Secure Online Services; paper IR4 may be used for non-myIR taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed and terminal tax paid by 7 July in the absence of a tax agent extension; Inland Revenue may grant an extension of time to file and pay under Part 4A of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1: Company identity and IRD jurisdiction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the New Zealand Limited company, New Zealand IRD number, registered office address, and principal officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and shareholders must be identified; the non-resident company should also enter the New Zealand-appointed agent for service of process, with full contact details. If no New Zealand agent is appointed, the return may be treated as ineffective and late-filing penalties can apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2: Accounting period and balance date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax year and balance date used for the return (standard year is 1 April to 31 March unless an alternative balance date is approved).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident entity's foreign accounting year must be aligned with the New Zealand income year for New Zealand-source income attribution. A mismatch does not defer New Zealand taxation; profit attributable to the New Zealand permanent establishment is taxable in the New Zealand year in which it is derived.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity and industry classification (ANZSIC/NZIAC code) for the cold storage warehouse operator.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The return should state 'Refrigerated logistics warehousing / cold storage for perishable pharmaceuticals' and identify whether the non-resident itself, rather than an offshore principal, is carrying on the New Zealand business through a fixed place of business. A foreign company that merely invoices from abroad but operates the warehouse in New Zealand creates a permanent establishment and must file this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All New Zealand-source gross income including cold storage rental fees, pallet in/out fees, temperature-controlled handling charges, insurance recoveries, and incidental storage and logistics revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers must declare all income sourced in New Zealand from the cold storage operation, even if the invoice is issued offshore. Amounts derived from storing pharmaceuticals physically located in New Zealand constitute New Zealand-source income; no deduction may be netted against gross income on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses necessarily incurred in deriving taxable New Zealand-source income: power, refrigeration electricity, wages, rent, maintenance, depreciation, insurance, freight, and apportioned head-office overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions for non-residents are limited to expenses attributable to New Zealand-source income. A non-resident may deduct only the arm's-length share of offshore head-office overheads that relate to the New Zealand permanent establishment; excessive management fees or IP royalty charges must be adjusted under transfer pricing rules and the general anti-avoidance rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses available to offset against current-year net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward indefinitely in New Zealand, but only where the company maintains at least 49% continuity of beneficial ownership from the start of the loss year through the end of the offset year. Non-resident share transfers of more than 51% extinguish the loss carry-forward and must be disclosed to Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7: Net taxable income or loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting allowable expenses and offsetting prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident company has no New Zealand permanent establishment and no New Zealand-source income, this line should be nil. If a permanent establishment exists, the entire profit attributable to New Zealand operations, including warehousing margins on intercompany cold storage service contracts, must be included here under Article 7 of the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8: Tax on taxable income at company rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated corporate income tax at the statutory rate applied to net taxable income, before tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 28% company tax rate. No reduced cold-storage concession applies. The non-resident must also ensure that transfer pricing adjustments do not leave artificially low New Zealand taxable profit; Inland Revenue may reconstruct the arm's-length storage margin under Income Tax Act 2007 sections GC 13 and GC 14.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9: Tax credits, RWT, imputation credits, and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits against income tax, including resident withholding tax on New Zealand interest and dividends, imputation credits attached to New Zealand dividends, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies do not generally claim New Zealand imputation credits on non-resident dividend withholding assessments unless a DTA expressly allows integration. Credits claimed must be supported by withholding certificates and must not exceed credits actually withheld. No credit may be claimed for NRWT on dividends if the dividend was not actually subject to NRWT because an exemption or DTA relief was applied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10: Net tax payable or refund due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax payable after all tax credits, or the refundable amount due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If domestic-rate NRWT was over-withheld because a DTA rate should have applied, the non-resident must separately pursue an administrative refund under Part 8 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 or file a corrective return. This line must never show a foreign tax credit against New Zealand tax for taxes paid in a treaty partner unless such credit is expressly available under the Income Tax Act 2007.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 triggers an initial NZD 250 penalty plus a further NZD 250 for each month or part-month the return remains outstanding, subject to Inland Revenue discretion and limitation periods. Late payment attracts an initial 1% late payment penalty, a further 4% after seven days, and an ongoing 1% per month thereafter. Substantial understatements attract shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for abusive tax positions, and up to 150% for evasion or similar conduct. Criminal fraud cases under sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act can result in fines up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment of up to five years for knowingly evading assessment or providing false documents.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% domestic non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid to non-residents, generally final, with reductions available under an applicable double tax agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident recipient must provide the New Zealand payer with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residence state's tax authority before payment, together with Inland Revenue Form IR67 (Certificate of Residence for non-residents claiming New Zealand tax relief) and a signed beneficial ownership declaration confirming that the recipient is the true owner of the income and is not a conduit. The payer must apply the treaty rate only after receiving the documentation; if the domestic 30% dividend or 15% interest/royalty rate has been withheld, the non-resident may claim a refund through Inland Revenue's annual return or IR67 process. All treaty claims must be supported by board minutes, underlying contracts, evidence of substantive economic activity in the residence state, and confirmation that the income is fully taxable in the residence state.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are subject to 15% domestic NRWT, with DTA-reduced rates commonly 10% or 0% depending on the treaty partner. Interest paid to non-residents is subject to 15% domestic NRWT, with DTA-reduced rates commonly 10% or 0%; approved bank issuers may instead elect to pay the 2% Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) where all conditions are met. Intercompany interest is also subject to transfer pricing and thin capitalisation adjustment risk.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10,000,000 aggregate annual value of cross-border related-party transactions generally triggers enhanced transfer pricing documentation expectations, including a Local File; New Zealand groups with consolidated revenue above NZD 1.1 billion are expected to prepare Master File and Country-by-Country Report documentation. No formal statutory de minimis exists, and Inland Revenue may request a full transfer pricing analysis for any related-party transaction regardless of size.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulations filing regime, but substance is decisive under the general anti-avoidance rule in Income Tax Act 2007 section BG 1 and under DTA permanent establishment analysis. For a temperature-controlled cold storage company, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) are the physical receipt, storage, temperature monitoring, inventory control, release, and hygiene management of perishable pharmaceuticals inside New Zealand. The entity must have real premises, employees, equipment, risk-bearing, and commercial control in New Zealand; a letterbox office or offshore invoicing shell cannot support profit allocation, treaty residence, or the arm's-length attribution of income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through mischaracterised fees and sham offshore invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The New Zealand cold storage company understates taxable income by paying a connected offshore shell company large 'technology royalties' or 'management fees' for fictitious temperature-monitoring IP, with no genuine personnel, no analysis of benefits, no contract substance, and no contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, while the New Zealand warehouse continues to operate and generate profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may invoke the general anti-avoidance rule under Income Tax Act 2007 section BG 1, reconstruct the arrangement under sections GC 13 and GC 14, impose a 100% to 150% shortfall penalty for evasion or similar conduct under the Tax Administration Act 1994, and prosecute criminally under section 143A for knowingly evading assessment, carrying a fine of up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment of up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced through the Companies Act 1993: directors who allow reckless or insolvent trading face personal liability under sections 135 and 136, and a court may order the director to compensate the company or the Commissioner under section 383 and order disqualification as a director. Inland Revenue may also apply to place a departure prohibition order (travel ban) under Part 11 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 until the tax debt and penalties are settled, and persistent serious breach can result in criminal imprisonment of the directing officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold and pay NRWT on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company declares and pays dividends to non-resident shareholders, pays royalty or interest to an offshore affiliate, or makes deemed distributions without deducting the applicable 30% dividend NRWT or 15% interest/royalty NRWT, and without first obtaining the required IR67 form and Tax Residency Certificate for DTA relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2007 and the Tax Administration Act 1994, Inland Revenue may assess the company for the full unpaid NRWT, add late payment penalties (1% initial, 4% after seven days, then 1% per month), and apply shortfall penalties for failing to take reasonable care (20%) or for an abusive tax position (40%). Criminal prosecution under section 143A may follow where the withholding omission was deliberate, with fines up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be made personally and jointly and severally liable for tax withheld or required to be withheld but not remitted to Inland Revenue under section 39A of the Tax Administration Act 1994. This personal liability attaches to the full unpaid NRWT plus penalties and interest. Directors may also face disqualification under the Companies Act 1993, civil restitution claims, departure prohibition orders, and criminal imprisonment where the failure was knowing and fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False permanent establishment declarations, sham foreign entity structure, and fraudulent record keeping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The non-resident parent or shadow director files an IR4 declaring that the New Zealand cold storage business is merely an agency or low-margin service provider and is not a permanent establishment, while in substance the New Zealand entity bears inventory risk, employs the workers, controls the cold chain, and earns the principal profit. The same conduct is aggravated by falsifying temperature-control logs, warehouse records, board minutes, or invoices to conceal the true economic owner of the operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Income Tax Act 2007 and Tax Administration Act 1994 authorise reassessment of the full New Zealand-source profit, cancellation of improper DTA relief, and criminal prosecution under section 143B for knowingly providing false or misleading information. The false-documentation offence carries fines up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years, while civil shortfall penalties can reach 150% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause the company to make false declarations are exposed to direct criminal liability as principals under the Crimes Act 1961, personal pecuniary penalties, contribution and compensation orders, disqualification under Companies Act 1993, and travel bans preventing departure from New Zealand. The court may order the directors personally to restore any tax shortfall and pay punitive damages where the sham structure was used to defeat public revenue.
